raw_response:
Hai, let me think about this year. I've been doing wheat-maize on this land for decades — my hands know what to do before my head catches up. Just me and the old man at home now, the kids are in the city and send money when they can. He helps when he's not doing odd jobs in town. 18 mu is manageable if I hire the machines at the busy times.

**Wheat (this winter's crop, planted last October? no — let me think forward to next October after I finish the maize cycle):** Wait, the question says start of growing season. In Quzhou the growing season really kicks off with maize in June after wheat harvest. My wheat is already in the ground from last October. So I'll plan the wheat I'm about to harvest in June, then the maize that follows, then the wheat I'll plant in October. Let me just lay out the full year.

For the wheat that's finishing up — I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base last October, and I'll topdress maybe 15 kg of urea at jointing in early March. That's about 16-17 kg of N per mu total, which is what the extension fellow said is reasonable and what I've done for years. Yield should be around 420 kg/mu if the spring isn't too dry. I'll irrigate three times — before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. Herbicide in early spring for weeds, I'm too old to be bending over pulling them. Maybe a fungicide spray at heading if powdery mildew shows up, like last year.

For maize right after — the window between wheat harvest mid-June and planting is tight, less than a week. I hire the no-till planter; can't afford to waste time plowing. Denghai hybrid seed, whatever the shop has that my neighbors are using. About 40 kg of compound fertilizer at planting plus maybe 10 kg urea topdress when it's knee-high. That's roughly 17 kg N/mu. I irrigate once or twice depending on the rain — the well costs money to run. Corn borer has been bad the last two years so I'll put granules in the whorl.

Then October, plant wheat again. Same variety, same pattern.

Labor — my husband and I do most of it, maybe 40 family days across both crops. I hire the combine for wheat harvest, the no-till planter for maize, and the maize harvester. That's maybe 5-6 hired days worth of machinery services. During weeding and spraying the two of us manage.
